answer.summary: Ivan Zhao recalled an investor sending dog treats to Notion’s office—even though its address wasn’t public—as an unexpected sign that investors were interested.

sections.heading: Unexpected sign of investor interest
sections.content: Zhao said that after Notion began earning revenue and its product started growing faster, investors began reaching out. One day, dog treats arrived at the office, whose address was not public. He later connected the gift to the team having posted on Twitter about hiring a dog at the office, and remarked that someone had tracked down the office address and followed them on Twitter. The unusual delivery made him pause and realize there was enough investor interest.

judgment.explanation: The answer accurately identifies the unexpected sign: dog treats were sent to Notion’s office despite its address not being public. It is supported by S2 and covers the expected point.
